steps.instruction: Start with a square. Fold the left edge to the diagonal from top left to bottom right.
Fold the top edge in to the same diagonal. The two folded edges meet along that line.
Press the creases flat to finish.
Start with a square sheet. Bring the top-left corner to the bottom-right corner and crease the fold.
Bring the upper-right tip down to the lower-left tip. Line up the corners to make a smaller triangle.
Press the creases flat to finish.
Bring the top left corner to the center.
Bring the top right corner to the center.
Bring the bottom right corner to the center.
Bring the final corner to the center to close the packet.
Press the creases flat to finish.
Fold the square diagonally.
Fold the upper point down to meet the bottom point.
Fold the left point over the layers. Slip a page corner between them.
Press the creases flat to finish.
Fold into a triangle.
Fold the bottom point inward to make a short base.
Turn the left tip inward to form a sail silhouette.
Press the creases flat to finish.
Fold the lower edge up, leaving a rim at the top.
Wrap the left edge inward.
Wrap the right edge inward. Tape the edges on the back to hold the pocket.
Press the creases flat to finish.
Start with a rectangle. Pinch the first narrow fold toward you.
Work across the sheet. Alternate folds toward and away from you.
Pinch one end of the accordion and wrap a paper band around it.
Spread the free end to open the fan.
Fold the left end inward.
Fold the right end over the left. Tape the back to keep the band closed.
Press the creases flat to finish.
Lay a paper strip about 16 × 5 cm horizontally. Fold its left end down along the dashed diagonal.
Fold the right end down along the second dashed line to form the other sloping edge.
Press the creases flat to finish.
Copy this net onto sturdy paper. Cut around its outside, including the small tabs.
Score the four dashed edges of the square base and the hinges of the corner tabs. Raise the side walls and turn the tabs inward.
Put glue on the four marked tabs. Press each tab against the inside of the neighboring wall and hold it until the glue grips.
Check that each glued joint is secure.
Copy this net onto sturdy paper. Cut around its outside, including the small tabs.
Score the panel edges. Fold along the dashed lines, keeping the tabs inside.
Glue the tabs to their neighboring panels and let them dry.
Check that each glued joint is secure.
Copy this net onto sturdy paper. Cut around its outside, including the small tabs.
Score only the dashed lines. Fold the three long panels around into a triangle, with the triangle ends and tabs facing inward.
Glue the tabs to their neighboring panels and let them dry.
Check that each glued joint is secure.
Start with a thin square sheet. Fold the top-left corner to the bottom-right corner.
Fold the triangle in half three more times in the order shown. Keep the center tip at the point of the narrow wedge.
Turn the wedge so the narrow tip points left. Trim the wide end and cut the marked notches. Leave the narrow tip intact.
Unfold the layers gently and flatten the rosette.
Fold the square corner to corner.
Fold the triangle in half, then again. Keep the center tip closed.
Cut the openings along the marked edge. Leave the center joined.
Unfold the layers gently and flatten the rosette.
Fold the square corner to corner.
Fold the triangle in half, then again. Keep the center tip closed.
Cut the openings along the marked edge. Leave the center joined.
Unfold the layers gently and flatten the rosette.
Fold the square corner to corner.
Fold the triangle in half, then again. Keep the center tip closed.
Cut the openings along the marked edge. Leave the center joined.
Unfold the layers gently and flatten the rosette.
Trace the first shape on colored paper and cut it out.
Trace and cut the remaining pieces. Lay them out before gluing.
Glue the pieces onto a folded card, from largest to smallest.
Trace the first shape on colored paper and cut it out.
Trace and cut the remaining pieces. Lay them out before gluing.
Glue the pieces onto a folded card, from largest to smallest.
Trace the first shape on colored paper and cut it out.
Trace and cut the remaining pieces. Lay them out before gluing.
Glue the pieces onto a folded card, from largest to smallest.
Trace and cut out two identical three-tiered pine tree silhouettes on sturdy card.
Cut a vertical center slot halfway down from the top peak on one tree and halfway up from the base on the other.
Stand the top-slotted tree upright and turn the second tree 90° directly above the slot.
Slide the upper tree straight down until both center slots lock flush into a four-winged 3D pine.
Cut out the hexagonal box net in one piece, keeping all six corner tabs and the lid tuck flap.
Score along the base hexagon and valley-fold the six walls up 90° while turning the corner tabs inward.
Glue each corner tab to the inside of its neighboring wall to lock the six-sided body.
Swing the hexagonal lid over the rim and slide the front tuck flap snugly inside the box.
Cut around the outer contour of the cottage net and slit the top and right edge of the front door.
Fold the two side walls and two pointed gable walls upright 90°, bending all corner and roof tabs inward.
Glue the four wall corner tabs inside the side walls so the cottage frame stands square.
Fold both roof slopes inward over the gable tabs and press the ridge seam shut.
Cut out the four-pointed star pyramid net, keeping the narrow glue tab on each triangle.
Score around the center square base and fold all four triangles and side tabs upward.
Apply glue to the four side tabs and bring the sloped edges together toward the top.
Press the last seam closed so all four tips meet cleanly at the pyramid apex.
Cut out the slanted wall net and the rectangular center divider strip with end tabs.
Fold the tall back wall, low front wall, and two sloped side panels upright 90°.
Glue the four side tabs inside the front and back walls to form a sturdy angled caddy.
Fold both end tabs on the divider 90° and glue it across the middle to create two compartments.
Cut out the eight-triangle fan net along its outer border, keeping all five edge glue tabs.
Score every interior triangle edge and valley-fold all creases inward to curve the facets.
Glue the upper closing tab first to form the top four-sided cone, then apply glue to the lower tabs.
Bring the four lower triangles together at the bottom tip and tuck a hanging ribbon into the top apex.
Cut the long cardstock strip with its narrow front lock tab and cut a matching center slit on the lip crease.
Valley-fold the two main frame creases inward and mountain-fold the front strip upward to form a cradle lip.
Bring the sloped backrest forward until the cradle crease meets the front edge of the base.
Insert the bottom lock tab through the front slit to brace the triangular easel without glue.
Cut out the five-pointed star net around its outer border, keeping a small tab on each arm.
Score around the inner pentagon base and fold all five star arms upward at an even 55° flare.
Fold the five side tabs inward and dab glue onto the outer face of each tab.
Press each tab behind the neighboring star arm until all five flared corners hold their dish shape.
Start with a square paper rotated like a diamond. Fold the top corner down to the bottom corner.
Fold the left corner downward at an angle to create the dog's left floppy ear.
Fold the right corner downward at the same angle to form the right ear.
Fold the bottom tip slightly upward to shape the snout.
Draw the eyes and a cute nose to complete your playful dog face.
Fold the top corner of the square diamond down so its tip touches the exact center.
Fold the bottom corner straight up until its tip meets the upper folded edge.
Fold the right side diagonally upward along the vertical center crease.
Fold the left side diagonally upward to meet the right side at the center line.
Fold the top peaks and side corners slightly backward to create smooth rounded curves.
Set the square like a diamond. Bring the top point to the bottom point along the dashed line.
Fold the left corner toward the upper center along the marked line. The corner should rise above the top edge.
Mirror the same fold on the right to make the second ear.
Fold a little of the bottom point upward so the chin has a straight edge.
Turn the paper over. Draw the eyes, nose and whiskers on the smooth side.
Fold the square diagonally in half into a triangle with the wide base at the bottom.
Bring the lower left corner straight across to the middle of the opposite right edge.
Bring the lower right corner across to the opposite corner of the left flap.
Fold the front triangular flap down over the rim to lock the cup walls.
Fold the back flap behind, then gently press the sides to open your sturdy paper cup.
Fold a rectangular sheet in half lengthwise. Cut off a narrow strip from the end for the handle.
Cut parallel vertical slits from the folded edge, stopping before reaching the open border.
Unfold the sheet flat to reveal the row of parallel cut slits along the center fold.
Roll into a cylinder, glue the side edges together, and attach the top handle.
Fold a paper sheet in half vertically to establish the symmetrical center spine.
Draw the half-profile of the butterfly with its body aligned along the folded spine.
Cut carefully along the wing contours through both layers, keeping the center fold intact.
Gently open the wings outward along the spine to display the symmetrical butterfly.
Fold a long paper strip back and forth into equal accordion pleats.
Draw half of a heart, extending the widest outer curve to touch the folded side edge.
Cut along the outline through all layers, leaving the side hinge tabs connected.
Gently stretch the pleats apart to reveal the continuous connected heart garland.
Fold the card in half and mark two parallel slit marks across the central crease.
Cut the two slits through the fold and score the tab back and forth.
Open the card to a 90° angle and push the tab forward to create a standing step.
Glue a decorative paper tent onto the pop-up step and mount inside an outer cover.
Prepare the backing card and glue a golden sun disc in the upper sky.
Cut out the distant mountain layer with sharp peaks and snowy summit ridges.
Cut the middle forest ridge in deep evergreen and the gentle foreground meadow.
Layer and glue the pieces from back to front to create rich atmospheric landscape depth.
Cut fine parallel fringes across a paper rectangle, leaving a solid band at the top.
Glue a folded paper hanging loop to the top corner of the uncut band.
Roll the uncut band tightly from left to right, wrapping the fringes into a round bundle.
Wrap a decorative collar around the neck and gently fan out the dangling fringes.
Cut multiple equal paper strips in alternating vibrant colors.
Curl the first strip into a round loop, overlap the ends, and glue them securely.
Slip a second strip through the first loop and glue its ends together to lock the link.
Continue adding alternating color strips to create a festive cascading paper chain garland.
Cut parallel longitudinal slits across a paper sheet, preserving a solid border frame.
Cut contrasting weft strips with the same width as the vertical warp bands.
Weave the first cross strip through the vertical slits in an under-and-over pattern.
Weave the remaining strips in alternating rows, pack them tightly, and secure the edges.
Cut out the four-triangle star net in one piece, keeping the three tapered side glue tabs.
Score around the center triangle and valley-fold all three triangular walls and side tabs upward.
Apply glue to all three side tabs and fold the walls inward so each tab tucks behind its neighbor.
Press all three seams together until the outer points meet cleanly at the tetrahedron apex.
Cut out both square nets: the deeper green base tray on the left and the slightly wider coral lid on the right.
Score all perimeter edges and valley-fold the four walls and corner tabs upward on both nets.
Glue all four corner tabs inside each adjacent wall to lock both the square base tray and the inverted lid.
Flip the finished lid upright and lower it straight over the box base until the rim seats cleanly.
Cut out the long rectangular tray net with its four side corner tabs and two end lock cuffs.
Score around the floor rectangle and valley-fold the long walls, corner tabs, and end walls upward.
Glue the four corner tabs and press the short end walls upright against them to form the frame.
Fold both end cuffs 175° inward over the inside walls to lock the corners and reinforce the tray ends.
Cut out the stepped bench net with both stepped side walls and the five glue tabs; note the red mountain crease on the second riser.
Valley-fold the front riser, lower tread, back wall, and side walls up while mountain-folding the upper riser upward.
Glue the step side tabs under the lower tread and apply glue along the upper tabs and back top tab.
Fold the upper seat tread backward onto the upper tabs and back top tab to seal the stepped bench.
Cut out the six-panel hexagonal tube strip with the full-length seam tab on the left edge.
Score all six parallel lines and valley-fold every panel and the seam tab inward to roughly 60°.
Run glue along the outside face of the seam tab while curling the left and right wings overhead.
Press the top panel down over the glued seam tab to close a symmetrical open-ended hexagonal tube.
Cut out the tabletop net with its four pinwheel aprons, L-shaped leg fins, and corner glue tabs.
Score all fold lines, fold the four aprons and legs upward, and fold each inner leg fin 90° to form L-posts.
Apply glue to the four apron corner tabs and press every apron wall to 90° inside its neighbor.
Flip the assembled table upright onto its four reinforced corner legs.
Cut out the roof canopy net with its four corner legs, leg fins, and front and back triangular collar braces.
Mountain-fold both roof slopes downward 36°, bend all four legs straight down, and turn each leg fin inward 90°.
Turn both collar brace glue tabs inward and apply glue along the slanted edges beneath the ridge.
Swing the front and back triangular collar braces under the canopy and glue them against the opposite slope.
Cut out the cross-shaped lantern net, four side stile tabs, and all four centered square window apertures.
Score around the gold center floor and valley-fold all four pierced walls and stile tabs upward.
Apply glue to the four side tabs and join the back, left, and front walls upright at 90° corners.
Close the fourth windowed wall squarely over the remaining corner tabs to complete the open-top lantern.
Cut out the tent net with its back gable wall, ridge tab, and two front triangular door flaps.
Valley-fold the two sloped walls and back gable upward while pre-creasing the front door flaps outward.
Apply glue to the ridge tab and back gable tabs, then join the sloped walls together along the peak.
Swing both hinged gold door flaps outward along the front edges to open the tent entrance.
Cut out the four-bay stepped surround strip with tapered shoulder miters, upper corner tabs, and one end seam tab.
Valley-fold the shoulder ledges and top rim collars inward while mountain-folding the four upper shaft walls upright.
Stand the surround upright, apply glue to the four upper tabs and base seam tab, and begin wrapping the four bays into a square.
Close the fourth corner seam and press all mitered shoulder and rim joints flush around the open center well.
Start with a vertical rectangular sheet. Fold the top edge down to meet the bottom edge.
Fold the top-left and top-right corners inward to meet along the center line, leaving a bottom strip.
Fold the front bottom strip up over the triangles, fold the back strip behind, and tuck the small side tips inward.
Open the hat pocket and flatten it into a diamond, then fold the front bottom point up to the top peak and repeat behind.
Open the bottom pocket again into a smaller diamond, then gently pull both upper outer flaps outward to open the hull.
Shape the side gunwales and press the bottom seam flat so your classic paper rowboat stands upright.
Rotate a square sheet like a diamond. Fold the top corner down to the bottom corner and unfold to mark the centerline.
Fold the upper-right and lower-right edges inward so both meet cleanly along the horizontal center crease.
Fold the left pointed tip inward along the vertical crease to shape the whale's rounded head.
Mountain-fold the lower half behind the upper half along the center crease so the inner flaps are hidden inside.
Fold the pointed tail end diagonally upward along the crease to raise the whale's tail fluke.
Draw an eye and a gentle smile near the front head to complete your paper whale.
Start with a square sheet rotated like a diamond. Fold the top corner down to meet the bottom corner.
Fold the left and right corners downward along the diagonal creases so both tips meet at the bottom point.
Fold both front lower triangular flaps straight upward so their points meet the top peak.
Fold the two front upper flaps outward at symmetrical angles to shape the helmet horns.
Fold only the front bottom triangle tip upward so its point touches the center horizontal line.
Fold the front brim band upward over the base, then fold the remaining back triangle up inside to finish the samurai hat.
Start with a vertical rectangular strip. Fold the top half straight down to meet the bottom edge.
Fold the top-left and top-right corners down through both layers so their edges meet along the center line.
Swing only the two front triangular flaps outward along the angled creases to form floppy dog ears.
Mountain-fold the top peak slightly backward along the dashed line to flatten the dog's forehead.
Draw the eyes, nose, and collar, then slide the open bottom sleeve over the top edge of a book page.
Start with a square rotated like a diamond. Fold the bottom corner straight up to meet the top corner.
Fold the left corner diagonally upward along the angled crease so its tip rises past the sloped top edge.
Mirror the opposing corner fold on the right side so both raised tips form symmetrical eye bumps.
Mountain-fold the center top peak backward along the horizontal crease to flatten the brow between the eyes.
Draw wide frog eyes on the raised flaps and a cheerful smile across the face to complete your frog.
Start with a square rotated like a diamond. Fold the bottom corner up to meet the top corner.
Fold the triangle in half from left to right and unfold to crease the vertical center guideline.
Fold the left corner diagonally upward from just left of the base midpoint to raise the left tulip petal.
Mirror the same angled fold on the right side to raise the right petal symmetrically.
Mountain-fold the two sharp outer lower corners slightly backward to round the base of the blossom.
Turn the blossom over to the smooth front side to reveal your finished three-petal tulip.
Start with a square rotated like a diamond. Fold the left corner inward so its tip touches the exact center.
Fold the right corner inward symmetrically so both triangular tips meet at the center seam.
Fold the bottom point straight upward along the lower dashed line to form the front pocket wall.
Fold the top triangular flap downward along the upper crease so its tip reaches into the pocket.
Slip the top triangular tip behind the front pocket lip to lock your neat diamond pouch closed.
Start with a square rotated like a diamond. Fold the left corner to the right corner and unfold to mark the center crease.
Fold both upper edges inward so they meet cleanly along the vertical center crease.
Mountain-fold the protruding bottom triangle backward along the horizontal crease to flatten the tent base.
Fold the two front center flaps diagonally outward along the dashed lines to peel open the tent doorway.
Gently spread the side panels apart so your folded camping tent stands upright on its triangular base.
Rotate a square like a diamond. Fold the top corner down to the bottom corner and unfold to crease the horizontal centerline.
Fold the upper-right and lower-right edges inward to meet neatly along the horizontal centerline.
Fold both left-side edges inward to the horizontal centerline as well, narrowing the paper into a slender diamond.
Fold the two front inner flaps outward across the dashed lines so their tips stand out as top and bottom fins.
Fold the slender right tail tip diagonally upward along the crease to shape the swimming tail fin.
Draw an eye and curved gill mark near the pointed head to complete your slender paper fish.
Start with a square sheet. Fold the bottom edge straight up to meet the top edge.
Fold the left and right edges inward to meet cleanly along the vertical center line.
Open both side pockets from inside and squash-fold them flat outward into symmetrical pointed side eaves.
Fold the upper front center flap downward along the dashed line to form the projecting keyboard shelf.
Fold both pointed side wings forward 90 degrees along the vertical creases to support the upright piano.
Draw white and black keys across the projecting shelf to complete your standing upright piano base.
Start with a square sheet. Fold both diagonals corner-to-corner and unfold to mark an X-shaped crease.
Fold the top edge down to the bottom edge, then push both side edges inward along the diagonal creases into a triangle.
On the front layer only, fold the top-left and top-right corners down so both tips meet at the bottom apex.
Turn the triangle over and fold the bottom point straight up past the top edge, gently curving the wings behind.
Fold the small protruding top tip downward over the upper edge to lock the center body, then flip back over.
Pinch a gentle mountain fold down the center spine so all four wings lift symmetrically without any cutting.
Start with a vertical rectangular sheet. Fold it in half from left to right and unfold to mark the center crease.
Fold the top-left and top-right corners inward so both top edges meet along the center crease.
Fold both angled front edges inward a second time to meet along the center line, shaping a sharp dart nose.
Fold the glider in half along the vertical center crease so the left and right wing halves align.
Fold the top wing outward along the vertical crease parallel to the bottom spine, then repeat on the other wing.
Lift both wings slightly above horizontal into a gentle V-angle so your paper glider flies smoothly.
Fold a wide rectangular sheet in half vertically so the right edge meets the left edge.
Accordion-fold both layers outward along the vertical quarter line into a four-panel stack.
Leave top and bottom rim bands uncut, then cut alternating horizontal slits from opposite sides.
Unfold flat to reveal the staggered slit grid, then curl the ends into a cylinder overlapping the right glue strip.
Glue the vertical seam and gently pull the top and bottom rims apart to expand the diamond lantern cage.
Fold a rectangular green sheet in half vertically to create the center leaf spine.
Draw half of a rounded-lobe oak leaf and basal stem anchored along the folded spine.
Cut along the lobed contour through both layers while keeping the folded center spine intact.
Unfold the cutout flat along the center crease to reveal the symmetrical oak leaf.
Fold a rectangular sheet in half vertically to form the center spine of the fish.
Sketch half of the fish outline—rounded head, swept side fin, pelvic fin, and forked tail—along the folded edge.
Cut carefully along the body, swept fins, and forked tail through both layers, leaving the center spine uncut.
Open the folded sheet flat to reveal the symmetrical mirrored fish cutout.
Fold a rectangular sheet in half vertically to establish the mushroom's center line.
Draw the domed cap, gill notch, and thick stem along the fold, plus a small half-circle on the upper spine.
Cut along the mushroom outline and snip out the small half-circle on the folded spine.
Unfold flat along the spine to reveal the symmetrical mushroom silhouette and center cap spot.
Start with a square sheet and fold the bottom-right corner up to the top-left corner.
Fold the triangle in half again so the two acute corners meet, leaving the center apex at the bottom point.
Cut straight from the closed center apex along both diagonal edges, stopping cleanly before the outer rim.
Unfold flat to reveal the centered X-slit, then fold one half of each triangular flap outward along the dashed lines.
Crease all four blades flat to frame the open fourfold pinwheel window.
Fold a long horizontal paper strip back and forth into four equal accordion pleats.
Draw a paper doll whose outstretched arms and hands touch both folded side edges.
Cut along the head, dress, and legs through all layers, leaving the outer hand edges uncut.
Unfold the accordion pleats gently to reveal four paper dolls holding hands in a row.
Accordion-fold a long strip back and forth into four equal vertical panels.
Fold the stacked accordion packet in half vertically so all centerlines align on the left spine.
Cut the upper and lower slopes leaving a side bridge tab uncut, then snip a small V-notch from the left spine.
Unfold all layers completely to reveal a continuous garland of connected open-center diamonds.
Start with a square sheet and fold it diagonally from corner to corner into a triangle.
Fold the triangle in half twice more into a narrow eight-layer wedge with the center point at the bottom.
Trim the outer edge into a rounded petal curve, then cut radial fringe slits stopping at the inner guide arc.
Unfold all layers flat and gently lift the fringe tips to bloom the radial paper fringe blossom.
Fold a square sheet in half from bottom to top.
Fold the strip in half from left to right so the closed center point sits at the bottom-left corner.
Cut a curved quarter-flower opening around the closed center corner, leaving the outer border intact.
Unfold both folds flat to reveal the crisp four-petal stencil window inside its square frame.
Fold a rectangular paper sheet in half vertically to form a double-layer strip.
Cut alternating horizontal slits from the open edge and the folded spine, stopping inside the margins.
Unfold flat to show the alternating side and center slits, then gently pull the top and bottom edges apart.
Stretch the sheet vertically so every alternating slit opens into an expandable diamond lattice.
Accordion-fold a long horizontal strip into four equal stacked pleats.
Leave a solid top header ribbon uncut across both folds and draw a three-scallop pennant below it.
Cut the side notches and scalloped lower contour through all layers while keeping the top ribbon joined.
Unfold the pleats smoothly to display the continuous four-flag scalloped paper bunting.
Fold a square sheet in half vertically so the left edge meets the right edge.
Cut one straight diagonal slit from the upper folded spine downward, stopping inside the side margin.
Unfold flat to reveal the inverted-V cut, then fold the triangular flap downward along the horizontal crease.
Press the folded triangular shutter flat to open the clean triangular window.
Draw the fish silhouette with its notched tail fin on blue cardstock and cut along the outline.
Cut contrasting paper strips into small uniform square tiles for the mosaic scales.
Dab glue dots inside the body contour, press mosaic tiles in neat rows, and crease three tail fin ribs.
Finish tiling the body with even spacing and glue a crisp paper eye near the nose.
Cut the sleeve net with side wrap flaps, a bottom seal tab, and a top thumb-notch.
Apply glue dots to the left flap and bottom tab, then fold both side flaps and the bottom tab behind to seal the sleeve.
Cut a slightly narrower inner insert card with a rounded top pull-tab, punched hole, and front emblem.
Slide the insert card straight down through the top opening so it nests cleanly inside the sleeve.
Pull the rounded top tab up and down to slide the inner emblem card smoothly inside its sleeve.
Cut four diagonal slits from the corners toward the center, leaving the inner hub solid, and punch center and alternating corner holes.
Curl the first punched corner tip gently inward without creasing so its hole sits over the center hub.
Repeat with the remaining three alternating corners in clockwise order, stacking all four holes at the center.
Push a center fastener through all four corner holes and into the top of a sturdy folded paper stem.
Lock the center fastener loosely enough for the four curved blades to spin freely on the stem.
Cut one long loop strip, one tail strip with V-notches at both ends, and one short collar band.
Curve both ends of the main strip inward to the center glue dot to form twin rounded bow loops.
Glue the V-notched tail strip beneath the pinched waist, then wrap the gold collar strip vertically around the center.
Glue the collar ends neatly behind the knot and shape both bow loops to finish.
Trim the top corners of a sturdy bookmark strip at a bevel and punch a hanging hole near the top.
Cut a golden sun disc, a wide pale-blue back cloud, and a smaller crisp white front cloud.
Glue the sun disc peeking behind the back cloud, then press the smaller white cloud over the lower front edge.
Mount the layered sun-and-cloud cluster onto the bookmark face and thread a short ribbon loop through the top hole.
Cut a beveled gift tag with a top punch hole, five pink quilling strips for petals, and one shorter yellow strip for the flower center.
Roll each petal strip into a loose coil, glue the tip, and pinch one side into a sharp teardrop; roll the yellow strip into a tight center disc.
Dab five radial glue dots on the tag face and arrange the five teardrop petals pointing toward the center.
Apply a glue dot where the petal tips meet and press the tight yellow spiral disc into the center.
Thread a tie cord through the top hole to finish your dimensional quilled flower gift tag.
Cut four identical teardrop balloon panels in alternating colors and one small trapezoid basket.
Fold each teardrop panel cleanly in half down its vertical centerline with colored sides facing inside.
Apply glue to the right half of Panel 1 and align Panel 2 back-to-back along the center spine; repeat for Panels 3 and 4.
Open the four glued ribs evenly and attach two suspension cords from the balloon collar down to the basket.
Press the cord ends securely inside the collar and basket rim to display your 3D paper hot-air balloon.
Cut a sturdy circular cardstock disc and punch two opposite string holes near the left and right edges.
Glue a peach star upright on the front face and a contrasting blue framing ring on the reverse face.
Thread a twine loop through each side hole and knot the ends to form left and right spin handles.
Wind both cords tightly and pull outward so the disc spins rapidly, optically blending the star inside the ring.
Overlap two contrasting strips at a 90-degree angle near the bottom and glue the diamond junction flat.
Fold the left blue strip straight across to the right along the crisp vertical crease over the gold strip.
Alternate folding the gold strip left and the blue strip right along crisp edge creases up the column.
Continue alternating folds to the desired length, trim the final tails flush, and glue the ends behind to finish.
Glue three contrasting paper strips side by side beneath a sturdy top anchor tab.
Cross the left peach strip diagonally over the center gold strip to start the plait.
Next, cross the right blue strip diagonally over the new center strip, keeping tension even.
Continue alternating left-over-center and right-over-center down the strip, then glue a matching bottom anchor tab.
Cut a long green border band and five narrow curling strips, folding a short glue foot at one end of each.
Roll each strip tightly around a dowel toward the folded foot, then release slightly into an open springy spiral.
Dab five evenly spaced glue dots along the green band and press each spiral's flat foot upright onto a dot.
Align all five alternating spiral curls side by side until the glue dries for a crisp border trim.
Mark a corner overlap square near one end of each strip and cut a halfway cross-slit on opposite edges.
Align the two half-width slits at 90 degrees and slide the vertical strip straight into the horizontal slit.
Lock the cross-lap joint flush, then fold both short overhanging end tabs neatly behind along the corner edges.
Press the locked cross-lap corner flat to finish a clean, glue-free interlocked L-corner border trim.
Cut out the outer box net (with low front wall and top rail flanges), the U-shaped inner runner liner, and the windowed sliding lid from 200 gsm cardstock.
Fold the outer walls and corner tabs up 90°, pre-crease the top side rail flanges inward, fold the runner ledges inward at 34 mm height, and turn the lid pull tab up 78°.
Glue the four outer corner tabs shut, glue the runner liner inside so both ledges sit at 34 mm height, and fold both top rail flanges 90° inward to form 12 mm side tracks.
Level the windowed display lid across the low front threshold and align its side edges inside the open gap between the gold runner ledges and blue top rails.
Slide the lid all the way back to the rear wall to close the display box, or pull the coral tab forward along the rails to open it.
Cut out the one-piece chair net on 200 gsm cardstock, including the three arched leg cutouts and the slits separating the armrests from the seat tabs.
Mountain-fold the front apron and both side seat tabs 90° downward, and pre-fold the side leg walls, rear lock tabs, and upright backrest inward.
Swing both side walls 90° backward into alignment and glue the two seat side tabs flush inside the left and right leg frames.
Raise the backrest upright to 90° between the gold armrest wings and glue both rear lock tabs flat against the back wall to brace the chair rigidly.
Cut out the gatehouse arch net and drawbridge leaf from 200 gsm cardstock, punch 3.5 mm axle holes 14 mm above the front corner of each pier, and cut a 13 cm bamboo skewer axle.
Fold both gatehouse piers up 90°, glue the overhead arch lintel across the piers, fold the bridge side curbs up 90°, and curl the three-part hinge barrel 270° under the rear edge.
Seat the drawbridge hinge barrel between the front pier holes and slide the wooden axle pin horizontally through the left pier, barrel, and right pier.
Swing the drawbridge leaf up into the hollow archway to close the gate and lower it back onto the axle to test smooth movement.
Cut out both pentagonal star nets from 200 gsm cardstock: the 48 mm-radius hollow prism body with five 106 mm walls and the 51.5 mm-radius removable cap with 25 mm skirt flaps.
Score around both center pentagons and valley-fold all five prism walls, cap skirt flaps, and corner glue tabs upward.
Glue the five prism corner tabs 75° inside their neighboring walls to close the hollow five-sided column, and glue all five cap skirt tabs into a rigid lid.
Flip the gold pentagonal cap upright, align its five corners with the prism rim, and slide it smoothly down onto the column.

Cut out the four-column strip (80 mm total wall width per bay, 6 alternating 16 mm pleat bands, and 11 mm end collars) from 140–160 gsm paper; score horizontal alternating mountain/valley lines and 45° corner diagonals.
Pre-fold the six horizontal mountain and valley creases flat like an accordion washboard, then unfold partially and score the four vertical corners.
Fold the four vertical wall columns 90° into an open-ended square tube, apply glue along the full-length side tab, and seal the fourth corner seam.
Pinch the four corner diagonal creases inward along every valley fold to collapse the bellows flat, then pull and release the gold collars to test accordion motion.
Cut out the eight-panel core strip (27 mm tall with 16 splayed petal tabs and one side seam tab) and two octagonal ring flanges (17 mm inner bore, 36 mm outer radius) from 200 gsm cardstock.
Fold the eight core panels 45° inward, glue the side seam tab into an octagonal drum, and mountain-fold all 16 petal tabs 90° outward like sunburst flanges.
Apply glue to both rings of outward petal tabs and press the first octagonal ring flange concentrically onto the bottom drum rim.
Center the second octagonal ring flange over the upper petal tabs and press flush around the open center bore to complete the shallow spool.
Cut out the notched twin-bracket base, the flanged plank net, and the square pivot axle strip.
Fold both notched brackets upright to 90 degrees, turn the beam rails down, and fold both end seat lips up.
Seat the axle bar under the beam center and lower it straight into the two bracket saddle notches.
Rock the tabletop seesaw back and forth on its brackets to check smooth, balanced pivoting.
Cut out the A-frame stand net, the four-blade mill rotor, and a small split-pin strip.
Fold the stand tower and rear brace upright into an A-frame, and angle each rotor vane flap forward.
Align the rotor hub on the upper stand wall and push the split-pin fastener through the center.
Spin the mill blades around the split-pin hub to verify smooth, unobstructed rotation.
Cut out the octagonal shallow base net, the central pivot collar, and both hexagonal caddy strips.
Fold the eight shallow base rim flaps upright and wrap both caddy sleeves into closed hexagonal cups.
Seat the wider caddy cup over the base pivot collar and stack the upper cup onto its shoulder deck.
Rotate the stacked two-tier caddy smoothly inside the shallow base to reach every compartment.
Cut out the four-wall periscope tower net with top and bottom window ports, flared foot tabs, and two reflective panels.
Fold the flared base flat and fold three tower walls upright, leaving the side access door open.
Slide both reflective panels (foil or mirror cards) into the upper and lower 45-degree slots facing each other, then close the side wall.
Trace the light path entering the top window, reflecting down the shaft between the two 45-degree panels, and exiting the eye port.
Cut out the two matching flat slotted crescent side walls and three slotted cross-ribs.
Stand both flat crescent walls upright parallel to each other and align the three cross-ribs above their slots.
Slide all three cross-ribs straight down into the crescent wall notches until the joints lock flush.
Tilt and release the crescent sculpture to test smooth side-to-side rocking along its curved base.
Start with a vertical 2:1 rectangle. Crease an X across the upper square and mountain-fold its horizontal midline, then collapse the sides inward into a triangle head.
Fold the left and right edges of the lower square inward to meet along the vertical center line, narrowing the frog's body.
Fold the two front flaps of the triangular head diagonally upward and outward to form the frog's front legs.
Fold the bottom section upward along the waist crease and flare both lower flaps diagonally outward to shape the hind legs.
Make a horizontal valley fold across the back and a mountain fold halfway back down to create an accordion Z-spring fold underneath.
Press the back edge of the Z-spring gently with your fingertip and release to make your origami frog leap forward.
Start with a square rotated like a diamond. Fold it in half from left to right and unfold to mark the vertical center crease.
Fold both lower sloped edges inward so they meet cleanly along the vertical center line, forming a kite shape.
Fold the outer lower edges inward to the center line a second time to create a long, slender neck.
Mountain-fold the narrow kite in half lengthwise along the center spine so the two outer halves meet behind.
Turn the folded shape horizontally with the long point to the left, then inside-reverse-fold the slender neck upward.
Inside-reverse-fold the tip of the neck forward to form the head and beak, then tilt the tail tip up so your swan stands tall.
Start with a square rotated like a diamond. Fold the bottom corner straight up to meet the top corner.
Crease the vertical center line, fold a narrow bottom cuff upward along the lower dashed line, and mountain-fold the top peak behind to form a flat forehead.
Fold the left and right lower corners diagonally upward from the center base so two tall ear points extend above the forehead.
Gently open each ear flap from its inner crease and squash-fold it outward into an open pocket ear revealing the inner layer.
Mountain-fold the bottom chin corner and both outer cheek corners slightly backward to round the rabbit's face.
Shape the open ear pockets gently with your fingertips and add eyes and a small nose to finish your pocket-ear rabbit.
Crease both diagonals as valley folds and the horizontal midline as a mountain fold, then push the left and right edges inward to collapse into a waterbomb base.
Fold the front left and right bottom corners straight up to meet at the top peak, then flip over and repeat on the back flaps.
Fold the left and right outer diamond points inward to meet along the vertical center line, and repeat on the back.
Fold the two loose top flaps downward and tuck each tip cleanly into the diagonal pocket directly below it; repeat on the back.
Locate the small air-pocket opening at the bottom point and blow gently inside while coaxing the folded ribs outward.
Pinch the four vertical ribs lightly to crisp up the corners so your inflatable waterbomb holds its airy geometric shape.
Start with a landscape rectangular sheet (about 3:2). Crease the horizontal center line and fold all four corners inward to meet along it.
Fold the top half cleanly downward onto the bottom half along the horizontal center crease to form a wide trapezoid.
Fold both outer top corners diagonally downward along 45-degree creases from the top midpoint so the inner edges meet at the vertical center.
Mountain-fold the diamond in half vertically along the center line so the two inner flaps close cleanly inside the outer pocket.
Pinch the two lower outer corners together between thumb and forefinger, leaving the inner air flaps loose, and snap downward briskly.
A sharp downward flick opens the loose inner pockets with a pop. Tuck the pockets back in to reset.
Crease both diagonals on a square sheet, then fold all four corners inward to meet cleanly at the center (blintz base).
Flip the folded diamond over and fold all four outer corners inward to the center a second time.
Fold each of the four inner center tips outward across the dashed bevel lines so their points extend just past the square rim.
Flip the disc over and pinch the four diagonal ridges upward to form a sturdy cross-shaped handle while pressing the center point underneath.
Pinch the upright cross handle between thumb and forefinger and flick to spin your origami top smoothly on its pointed base.
Start with a 2:1 horizontal strip. Crease four equal panels plus a narrow right tuck tab, then fold the bottom third upward to form a sturdy headband rim.
Along the top edge, crease 45-degree V-lines down to each panel divider and fold the small corner triangles inward to reveal four sharp crown peaks.
Reverse-fold the V-notches inward as you bend the four panel dividers backward 90 degrees to curve the crown into a ring.
Slide the narrow right headband end straight inside the open pocket of the left headband cuff to lock the crown firmly closed.
Crease the four corner edges lightly outward so your four-point paper crown stands upright and holds its regal shape.
Start with an uncut square rotated like a diamond. Crease the diagonals and fold all four corners inward to meet at the center.
Fold the left and right edges inward to meet cleanly along the vertical center line, creasing the side wall lines.
Fold the top and bottom edges inward to meet at the horizontal center to crease the end-wall folds, then unfold the top and bottom triangular flaps completely open.
Lift the two side walls upright, pinch the corner creases inward to wrap around the ends, and fold both pointed end flaps down into the tray floor.
Press the two end-flap tips flat against the floor of the tray to lock the four walls upright.
Start with a vertical rectangular sheet. Fold the bottom edge upward about two-thirds of the height to form the envelope pocket.
Mountain-fold narrow vertical side margins backward to lock both pocket edges, and fold the top corners diagonally inward to shape a pointed flap.
Fold the top rim of the front pocket down and pleat it back up along the dashed lines to create a raised horizontal tuck-lock band.
Fold the pointed top flap straight downward and slide its triangular tongue securely behind the horizontal tuck-lock band.
Press the horizontal tuck band flat across the tucked flap so your letter envelope locks securely without glue or tape.
Start with a square rotated like a diamond. Fold all four corners inward to meet cleanly at the center.
Fold each of the four inner center tips outward along the dashed border lines to open a centered square photo window.
Mountain-fold all four protruding triangle tips cleanly behind the outer frame edges to lock the mitered border rails.
Slip a square photo behind the window flaps and pull one folded rear tab slightly outward as a tabletop stand.
Crease the four corner seams crisp and set your framed artwork upright on its rear paper stand.
Start with a landscape rectangle. Fold narrow 1/10-height hems inward along both the top and bottom edges to reinforce the center dispensing lips.
Fold the hemmed top and bottom edges inward to meet cleanly along the horizontal center line, forming the dispensing slot.
Crease two parallel accordion gusset lines near each short end, miter the four outer corners inward, and fold the end tabs over the front.
Tuck the mitered corners of both end tabs underneath the reinforced center hem cuffs to lock the collapsible pouch closed.
Pull the front and back walls apart along the accordion side gussets to expand your packet around tissues—it collapses flat again when empty.
Start with a 4:1 horizontal strip. Fold both long edges inward to the horizontal center line, then fold the strip in half lengthwise into a sturdy band.
At the exact center of the band, fold both arms diagonally upward and back out along 45-degree creases to raise a faceted diamond crest.
Taper the right tip slightly by folding its corners inward, then curve both band arms smoothly downward into a finger-sized circle.
Slide the tapered right band tip about one finger-width inside the open layered pocket of the left band end to lock the ring.
Adjust the tucked overlap slightly to fit your finger size and crisp the facets on top of your origami crest ring.
Start with a square rotated like a diamond. Fold left to right and unfold to mark the vertical center line.
Fold the lower-left and lower-right edges inward to meet cleanly along the vertical center line, forming a kite shape.
Fold the upper outer edges inward to meet at the center line, then narrow the lower outer edges inward as well to form a slender diamond stalk.
Mountain-fold the slender diamond in half vertically along its spine, then fold the lower point diagonally upward from near the base to raise the tulip leaf.
Crease the angled leaf spine firmly so your tulip stem stands upright—its tapered top tip fits neatly into the base of a folded tulip blossom.
Start with a vertical 2:1 rectangle. Fold both long left and right edges inward by about one-sixth width to form sturdy side sole rails.
Fold the top section downward along the upper dashed line to create the closed-toe sandal upper facing the heel.
Mountain-fold both top corners backward to round the toe and tuck the lower side edges of the upper flap neatly inside the sole side cuffs.
Mountain-fold both bottom heel corners slightly backward to contour the heel, and gently arch the open instep pocket upward.
Shape the arched toe pocket smoothly with your fingers so your origami slip-on sandal holds its sculpted 3D profile.
Fold a rectangular card in half horizontally so the bottom edge meets the top edge, forming a crisp lower spine.
From the folded bottom spine, cut four parallel vertical slits of increasing depth (10%, 18%, 28%, and 28% of sheet height) and crease horizontally between each pair.
Crease each stepped tab sharply forward and backward, then unfold the main card to 90 degrees while pushing all three steps inward.
Open the card to a right angle so the three square-cornered steps lock forward into a crisp 3D staircase.
Accordion-fold a wide rectangular strip back and forth into six equal vertical pleats, leaving a narrow right-end glue tab.
Leaving solid top and bottom rim bands, cut three small V-notches into the left fold edge and two staggered V-notches into the right fold edge.
Open the pleats partway to reveal staggered diamond windows centered along the ribs, then curve the ends together and glue the end tab.
Stand the joined fluted ring upright so the pleated walls hold an open, self-supporting lattice cylinder.
Start with a circular paper disc, punch a small suspension hole at the exact center, and trace a smooth inward spiral leaving a central hub.
Cut continuously along the spiral line from the outer rim inward, stopping around the central hub so the suspension point remains intact.
Knot a thin thread through the center hole and lift the hub straight up so the spiral coils begin to drop under their own weight.
Hang the spiral mobile from its center point so the continuous paper ribbon cascades into a balanced floating helix.
Fold a square sheet in half vertically so the left edge meets the right edge along a crisp center spine.
Cut the upper and lower background windows around the half-pumpkin contour, leaving the outer frame and green-marked stem, cheek, and base bridges uncut.
Cut the triangular eye, half-nose along the spine, and half-tooth mouth openings through both folded layers.
Unfold flat to reveal the glowing jack-o'-lantern face anchored cleanly inside its intact square window frame.
Fold a square sheet in half vertically so the left edge meets the right edge along a crisp center spine.
Cut top and bottom horizontal slits 60% toward the open edge, cut along the folded spine between them, and crease the vertical hinge line.
Unfold flat to reveal the centered H-shaped cut, then swing both rectangular shutters outward along their left and right hinges.
Crease both hinges sharply so the twin shutters stay flared open around the centered window aperture.
On heavy cardstock, cut four graduated arch slices and two equal base rails, adding matching half-depth vertical slots at identical spacing.
Line up the four graduated slices from front to back so each pair of bottom slots meets the four matching rail slots cleanly.
Push each slice straight down into the rail slots until its top edge locks flush with the rail surface.
Seat all four slices firmly onto both parallel rails to stand the layered 3D slice display upright.
Fold a square sheet in half horizontally and then in half vertically into a compact quarter-square with its closed center corner at the bottom-left.
Cut three evenly spaced L-shaped slits alternating from the left fold and bottom fold, stopping short of the opposite fold to preserve narrow hinge bridges.
Unfold flat to reveal the nested square rings joined by alternating horizontal and vertical bridges, then lift the center square gently.
Pull the center square upward so each concentric ring pivots smoothly on its alternating bridges into a 3D expanding square pyramid.
Fold a vertical rectangular sheet in half lengthwise so the left edge meets the right edge.
Cut the innermost arch window completely out, then cut the middle and outer arch tops, bottom sill, and spine, leaving the dashed vertical jamb lines uncut as hinges.
Unfold flat to open the central arch doorway, then swing the outer arched doors outward along their outer vertical hinges and fold the inner arch wings forward.
Angle both pairs of nested arch doors symmetrically forward to frame the layered central gateway.
Accordion-fold two equal narrow strips back and forth into matching four-pleat side walls.
Cut three equal square cards and pierce progressively smaller centered rectangular windows through them (largest in front, smallest at back).
Glue the left and right edges of each frame card onto matching front, middle, and back pleat peaks of the two accordion rails.
Pull the front and back panels gently apart so the accordion side walls expand into a deep 3D paper tunnel.
Stack six strips together and cut six identical curved wheel-arc segments with matching inner and outer radii.
On every segment, cut one half-width radial slit inward from the outer rim on the left end and one half-width slit outward from the inner rim on the right end.
Slide the inner slit of each new segment into the outer slit of the previous segment at 60-degree steps around the circle.
Tuck the sixth segment into the first segment's outer slit to lock the self-supporting interlocking paper wheel.
Fold the left and right quarters of a wide sheet inward so both outer edges meet cleanly along the center vertical line.
With both gatefold flaps closed, cut mirrored three-tier corner steps at the top and bottom plus two half-diamond notches along each meeting edge.
Swing both stepped wings outward along the side creases to reveal the solid center panel framed by symmetric terraced silhouettes.
Stand the decorative stepped gatefold open at a 60-degree wing angle so the symmetrical terraced doors frame the center stage.
Accordion-fold a long rectangular strip back and forth into twelve narrow, crisp pleats of equal width.
Cut a pointed peak across the top of the folded pleat stack and snip small triangular notches along both sides, leaving the bottom hub intact.
Fan the notched pleats open into a full circle, gather the bottom edge at the center, and glue the first and last pleats together.
Press the joined pleats gently flat into a circular 3D starburst medallion with crisp diamond cutouts.
Accordion-fold a long horizontal strip back and forth into four equal vertical panels.
Sketch a symmetrical pine tree across the folded panel so both its lowest bough tips and flat base extend all the way to the left and right fold edges.
Cut along the tree crown and trunk notches through all four layers, leaving the green-marked branch and base bridges uncut.
Unfold the accordion pleats partway into a sturdy zig-zag so the row of connected pine trees stands upright on its linked bases.
Start with a semicircular sheet and fold it radially in half three times around the bottom center point into a narrow eight-layer wedge.
Trim a curved scallop along the outer rim and cut staggered curved crescent notches from both radial folds, leaving solid ribs between openings.
Unfold the radial wedge layers gently one fold at a time as the curved notches open into symmetrical almond apertures.
Open the entire semicircle flat to display the symmetrical fan of radiating curved apertures.
Fold a sturdy rectangular backing card cleanly in half along the center crease, then open it upright.
Cut a four-band rainbow arch with two rectangular bottom support tabs, score the tab lines and center crown, and cut two clouds.
Crease both support tabs inward at 90 degrees and glue them onto opposite card wings slightly closer together than the flat arch.
Glue a layered paper cloud cleanly over each support tab to hide the joints and frame the rainbow base.
Flex the center crease gently when closing the card so the rainbow folds flat and pops upright whenever opened.
Cut a sturdy cardboard clock dial with 12 radial hour marks, a short hour hand, a long minute hand, and punch pivot holes through all three.
Stack the short hour hand beneath the long minute hand at the dial center and insert a brass split-pin brad through all aligned holes.
Flip the dial over and bend the two brass split-pin prongs flat in opposite directions, leaving slight slack so both hands spin smoothly.
Turn the clock face up and rotate the hour and minute hands independently around the brass pivot.
Cut one solid sky panel, two square tree-cutout frames with evergreen silhouettes, and four scored spacer strips.
Fold each spacer strip back and forth into a tight Z-spring and glue two spacers along the left and right edges of the sky panel.
Glue the middle tree frame onto the back spacers, attach the second spacer pair along its side borders, and align the foreground frame in front.
Press all stacked layers gently until the spacer glue sets, revealing deep 3D woodland perspective inside the shadow box.
Cut a rectangular body band wide enough to wrap around one finger with a glue tab, plus two pointed ears, a chest bib, and a tail.
Glue the ears above the face, attach the white cheeks, nose, and chest bib onto the flat band, and attach the tail on one edge.
Roll the illustrated band gently around a finger into an open tube and glue the side tab neatly along the back seam.
Slip the finished hollow cylinder onto your finger and curve the ears and tail gently outward.
Cut one wide torso strip marked with 8 equal pleat creases, plus a frog head, two arms, and two webbed feet.
Fold the wide torso strip back and forth in alternating valley and mountain pleats to form a bouncy paper accordion.
Glue the frog head and side arms onto the top flat pleat, and glue both webbed feet beneath the bottom pleat.
Let the glue set, then press and release the frog head gently to bounce the accordion spring body.
Fold a card blank in half along the left spine, then mark three front windows with uncut top hinges and cut lines on the other three sides.
Cut along the left, bottom, and right sides of each window, then fold all three flaps upward along their top hinges.
Dab glue around the outer border of an inner backing sheet (never on the flaps), add surprise motifs inside each window zone, and align the front panel on top.
Press the outer border edges firmly flat, then lift each hinged window flap upward to reveal the hidden pictures.
Measure and cut long narrow triangle strips (about 2 cm wide at the base tapering to a 18 cm point) in alternating colors.
Wrap the wide base tightly around a thin wooden skewer, roll smoothly toward the point, and dab white glue on the final tip to lock the bead.
Brush a light coat of clear glue to harden each bead, slide them off the skewer once dry, and thread them onto a strong cord.
Arrange alternating rolled beads along the cord and tie a secure double knot at the ends to wear your necklace.
Cut two identical scalloped medallions from stiff cardstock: cut one center slit halfway down from the top and the other halfway up from the bottom, plus a top hanging hole.
Hold the two medallions perpendicular and slide the bottom-slit piece straight down into the top-slit piece until the cuts lock flush.
Spread the four intersecting vanes evenly at 90-degree angles and tie a hanging cord loop through the top pinhole.
Suspend the finished ornament by its cord so all four interlocking panels catch light and spin gently.
Cut six vertical blue warp strips and six horizontal gold weft strips of equal width (about 1.5 cm wide by 18 cm long).
Line up the six warp strips side by side and weave row 1 over-2, under-2, over-2; shift row 2 by one strip (under-1, over-2, under-2, over-1) to begin the diagonal twill step.
Continue shifting each new weft row by one strip to build diagonal bands, pack tightly, then fold and glue all overhanging strip ends behind the square border.
Press the woven square flat under a book until the tucked edge tabs dry to finish a sturdy 2-over-2 twill coaster.
Overlap one end of two long contrasting strips (about 2 cm wide) at a crisp 90-degree L-corner and glue the corner square flat.
Fold the horizontal peach strip straight across to the left over the gold strip along the corner square edge.
Next fold the vertical gold strip straight up over the square, then keep alternating left-right and up-down folds until both strips run out and glue the final top square.
Trim any overhanging tail tips flush and stretch the folded stack gently upward into a bouncy square accordion spring.
Cut five equal peach paper strips (about 1.5 cm by 12 cm), one white circular backing hub, and one contrasting golden center disc.
Bend each strip into a teardrop loop, overlap both ends cleanly at the pointed tip, and glue the tips shut without creasing the round outer curve.
Dab five evenly spaced glue dots around the white backing disc and press all five teardrop petal tips onto the hub.
Glue the golden center disc firmly over the joined petal tips to complete the five-loop ribbon flower.
Start with one long narrow strip (about 1 cm by 25 cm) and tie a loose, flat overhand knot near one end.
Pull the knot evenly until it flattens into a crisp pentagon, fold the short tail along the edge, and tuck its tip into the pocket.
Wrap the long working strip flat around the pentagon following each edge angle until only a tiny tip remains, then tuck the tip inside the nearest flap.
Pinch the midpoint of each flat pentagon edge gently inward toward the center to pop the five star points out.
Shape all five puffed ridges evenly between your fingers to finish a crisp 3D lucky star.
Cut pairs of wide strips scored into five equal squares (four faces plus one tuck flap) for each cube, plus narrow connector strips.
Fold the blue strip into a hollow square frame and tuck its fifth square inside, then wrap the gold strip perpendicularly around it and tuck its flap shut into a fitted cube.
Slip a narrow connector strip under the outer wrap band of the first cube, loop it under the second cube's band, and glue the hidden ends inside the sleeve.
Link additional fitted paper cubes in alternating colors to form a crisp geometric 3D cube chain.
Cut one long peach hinge strip scored at the center and both outer quarters, plus two stiff blue panel strips to join.
Fold both outer quarter ends 180 degrees inward and glue them flat to form stiff doubled-ply ends flanking a flexible single-ply center crease.
Dab glue onto both doubled hinge ends and mount the two panel leaves flush up to the center crease without gluing over the fold line.
Flex the panels open and closed along the center crease—the doubled ends reinforce the glued joints against tearing.
Glue four contrasting strips (about 1.2 cm wide) side by side beneath a sturdy white top anchor tab.
Cross the outer-left peach strip over its neighbor toward the middle, and slip the outer-right green strip under its neighbor toward the middle.
Cross the right-center strip over the left-center strip to lock the middle weave, then repeat outer-in and center-cross down the strip.
Keep the outer edge folds crisp and even, then trim the ends flush and glue a matching bottom anchor tab.
Weave four vertical and four horizontal gold strips (about 1.5 cm wide by 24 cm long) one-over-one at the center to build a tight 4x4 square base.
Crease all sixteen protruding strip arms sharply upward 90 degrees along every edge of the 4x4 square base to form upright wall spokes.
Weave three horizontal blue strips continuously around all four upright walls over-and-under the spokes, creasing crisp corners and gluing ends inside.
Fold all protruding spoke tips neatly down over the top blue row, then wrap and glue a folded peach rim band around the entire top perimeter.
Press the folded rim firmly around all four corners to lock the woven square walls and solid base into a sturdy desk basket.
Cut out the single-piece wedge bookend net (77 × 64 mm base, 92 mm vertical back wall, 120 mm sloped brace, two right-triangle side walls, and five tuck tabs) from 240 gsm cardstock.
Valley-fold the vertical back wall and both triangular side cheeks 90° upright, and pre-fold all five side and crest tabs 90° inward.
Apply glue to the vertical back-wall tabs and press the triangular side cheeks flush against them to square the 90° rear corner.
Swing the sloped brace panel up 130° over the triangular cheeks and tuck the side and crest tabs inside the back wall to lock the rigid bookend.
Cut out the three-panel framed screen net (each wing 54 × 99 mm with cream window panels) and two triangular foot-bracket strips from 220 gsm cardstock.
Stand the center panel upright, valley-fold the left wing 54° forward, and mountain-fold the right wing 54° backward into a zigzag.
Fold each foot-bracket strip along its twin parallel creases into a sturdy triangular prism saddle.
Seat the lower corners of both screen hinges onto the two slotted triangular foot brackets to lock the freestanding zigzag divider.
Cut out the picture frame net (86 × 106 mm with lower card ledge and front lip) and the three-panel triangular strut net (27 mm face width with floor-tie strip and top tongue) from 250 gsm cardstock.
Fold the three strut panels 120° each and glue the side seam tab inside to form a rigid hollow triangular prism column.
Fold the picture frame's lower card ledge 90° forward and turn up the front retaining lip 90° to form a resting shelf.
Lean the picture frame back 18° onto the strut's flat floor-tie strip to set the base spacing.
Tilt the triangular strut forward to brace the upper back rail and fold its top locking tongue flush against the frame rear to complete the 72° stand.
Cut out the V-trough bookmark cradle net (94 × 70 mm back plate with 26 mm front lip and two triangular side cheeks) and the hinged base-stand net from 220 gsm cardstock.
Fold the front trough lip and both triangular side cheeks 90° forward, then glue the cheek tabs underneath the trough lip to form a rigid open cradle.
Fold the base stand's front catch rail 90° upright and swing the rear hinged kickstand prop forward with its top tongue bent back.
Seat the V-trough cradle behind the front catch rail and press the kickstand tongue flush against the back of the cradle to lock the 62° reading angle.
Cut out the six-panel diffuser strip (45 × 100 mm framed panels with cream window panes, 12 rim tabs, and one side seam tab) and two hollow hexagonal collar rings from 200 gsm cardstock.
Valley-fold the six framed wall panels 60° at each vertical crease and glue the side seam tab inside to close the open-ended hexagonal shell.
Valley-fold all six upper rim tabs and six lower rim tabs 90° inward to form flat interior collar ledges.
Seat the bottom hexagonal collar ring beneath the lower tabs and press the upper hexagonal crown ring flush onto the top ledges to lock the lantern diffuser shell.

Cut out the A-frame rain gauge stand net (77 × 99 mm faceplate with five graduated rainfall arc bands, floor base, and rear prop), the pointer needle, and a brass split-pin brad from 240 gsm cardstock.
Center the pointer needle over the dial pivot and push the brass split-pin brad cleanly through both holes from the front.
Flip the faceplate over and splay the two brass split-pin prongs flat in opposite directions, leaving slight slack so the needle turns smoothly.
Fold the gauge faceplate upright at a 72° lean, swing the rear prop leg forward, and tuck its top locking tongue behind the faceplate.
Sweep the indicator needle across all five graduated rainfall bands to check smooth rotation on the freestanding dial stand.
Cut out the three-panel triangular sleeve net (100 mm face width, 115 mm long with side glue tab) and the eight-segment corrugated flute strip from 220 gsm cardstock.
Accordion-fold the eight-segment strip along alternating mountain and valley creases (±132°) to compress it into a four-peak triangular truss core.
Fold the three outer sleeve panels 120° each and glue the side seam tab inside to form a hollow equilateral triangular prism.
Slide the pleated corrugated core lengthwise inside the triangular prism floor until nested cleanly, stiffening the beam against compression.
Cut out the eight-panel stair-stepped riser strip (96 mm wide with 22 mm risers, 27 mm treads, and 67 mm rear wall) and two stepped side cheek walls from 240 gsm cardstock.
Pleat the riser strip along alternating 90° valley and mountain creases to form a three-tier staircase with a vertical rear drop wall.
Fold the bottom foot flanges and rear locking tabs of both stepped side cheek walls 90° inward.
Apply glue to the inward cheek flanges and press both stepped side walls flush against the left and right ends of the staircase strip to complete the carton display.
Start with a 15 x 5 cm rectangular paper strip. Valley-fold the top and bottom edges inward to meet along the horizontal centerline.
Fold both outer ends diagonally downward at 45 degrees along the dashed creases to form two upright support legs.
Pinch a valley fold at the exact center and two mountain folds beside it to shape a V-groove chopstick cradle across the bridge.
Stand the rest upright on its two angled legs with the V-shaped center cradle facing upward to hold a pair of chopsticks.
Start with a 21 x 14 cm landscape rectangle. Valley-fold the bottom strip up by 1.5 cm to form a floor pocket, and fold small corner bevels at the top.
Crease three parallel horizontal valley folds: one narrow tuck tab near the top, the center ridge line, and the lower base fold.
Fold the back wall, floor, and front panel into a triangular tent, then slide the beveled front tab into the floor cuff pocket to lock the base.
Press the top ridge and locked base corners flat so your one-sheet name tent stands firmly on a desk.
Start with a 15 x 15 cm square sheet. Valley-fold the bottom edge upward to two-thirds of the height to form a deep seed pouch.
Fold both left and right vertical side strips inward across the front pouch to seal the sides and create two vertical cuff pockets.
Fold the upper-left and upper-right corners diagonally inward toward the top center so the pointed lid is narrower than the pouch.
Fold the tapered lid straight downward across the pouch rim and tuck both angled wing corners underneath the left and right side cuffs.
Press the vertical side cuffs flat over the tucked lid wings so your seed packet stays sealed without tape or glue.
Start with a 15 x 15 cm square. Crease both centerlines, then fold all four corners inward to meet cleanly at the center.
Turn the folded diamond over to its smooth side and fold all four corners inward to the center a second time.
You now have eight triangular inner score sections. Mountain-fold the square in half horizontally and vertically, then unfold to loosen the hinges.
Fold the square in half with the eight score sections inside, then slip your thumbs and index fingers into the four outer square pockets.
Pinch the four finger pockets together and flex them open to reveal all eight inner score sections.
Start with a 15 x 15 cm square. Crease both centerlines, then valley-fold the top and bottom edges inward to meet along the horizontal center.
Fold the left and right edges inward to meet at the vertical centerline, forming a compact four-pocket square.
Open each corner pocket from the center and squash-fold the upper pair upward and the lower pair downward into twin triangular peaks.
Mountain-fold the inner edge of the right sail behind to separate a shorter foresail, and fold the bottom peak upward to raise the hull.
Mountain-fold the lower-left and lower-right hull corners backward along the angled creases to taper the catamaran's bow and stern.
Slightly cup both sails and spread the twin-layered hull underneath so your two-sail catamaran stands steady.
Start with a 15 x 15 cm square rotated like a diamond. Crease the vertical center line, then fold both lower edges inward to meet along it.
Fold the top triangular peak straight downward across the brow line to create the owl's flat crown and pointed beak.
Fold both protruding side shoulder corners diagonally upward above the brow line to raise two horned owl ear tufts.
Mountain-fold the lower side edges backward to round the folded wings, then valley-fold the bottom point slightly upward to form a perch base.
Fold the small tip of the upturned tail flap back down slightly so it creates a stable flat ledge at the base.
Add two round eyes beneath the brow and gently open the side wing layers so your horned owl sits upright.
Start with a 15 x 15 cm square rotated like a diamond. Crease the vertical center line, fold all four outer edges to the center to form a Fish Base, and pinch out the two side waist flaps.
Angle the two side rabbit-ear flaps downward as front flippers, then mountain-fold the Fish Base in half lengthwise along the vertical center spine.
Turn the model horizontally with the flippers underneath. Inside-reverse-fold the left tip steeply upward for the neck and the right tail tip upward for the fluke.
Inside-reverse-fold the top tip of the neck forward to round the seal's head and snout, and gently flare the two side flippers outward.
Add a small eye dot and adjust the angled front flippers and tail fluke so your origami seal balances cleanly.
Start with a 15 x 15 cm square. Pre-crease a 4 x 4 grid, then valley-fold all four outer corners inward to touch the inner grid corners.
Fold the top mitered flap downward along the upper grid line, then fold the right flap leftward over it to lock the top-right corner.
Fold the bottom mitered flap upward over the lower half of the right flap to lock the bottom-right corner.
Fold the final left flap rightward over the bottom flap, and slip its upper mitered wing underneath the first top flap to complete the cyclic lock.
Press all four interlocked quadrants flat so the square coaster holds its crisp woven lock without glue.
Start with a 15 x 15 cm square rotated like a diamond. Crease the center vertical vein, then pinch two narrow accordion pleats radiating upward from near the bottom point.
Pleat the outer left and right corners slightly forward and upward along short diagonal creases to form the lower pair of lateral maple lobes.
Mountain-fold the lower-left and lower-right bottom edges backward toward the center line to narrow the base into a slender stem.
Pinch two tiny diagonal crimps along the upper central lobe shoulders and sharpen the radiating leaf-vein pleats.
Gently open the pleated ribs so the broad five-lobed maple leaf holds crisp dimensional facets above its slender stem.
Start with a 15 x 15 cm square. Valley-fold both diagonals and mountain-fold both centerlines, then collapse the side corners inward into a diamond Square Base.
Crease both lower edges inward to the center and the top triangle down, unfold them, then lift the front bottom corner upward into a tall Petal Fold and repeat on the back to form a Bird Base.
Fold the outer edges of the two slender lower points inward to meet along their centerlines on both the front and back layers.
Inside-reverse-fold both narrow lower points upward between the body layers to raise the crane's long neck on the left and tail on the right.
Inside-reverse-fold the tip of the neck forward and downward to form the head and beak, then fold both central triangular wings down.
Gently pull the neck and tail slightly apart to puff the central body so your finished origami crane opens its wings.
Lightly fold an 18 cm square cardstock sheet in half vertically and cut a centered U-shaped window from the folded spine, leaving a 4 cm border all around.
Unfold the frame flat and snip five evenly spaced parallel slits along each border rail, keeping solid uncut bridges along both the inner and outer edges.
Cut four 1.5 cm contrasting paper strips and thread them over and under through each border's slits, tucking the strip ends behind the corner bridges.
Finish weaving the left and right borders and pull all four strips taut so the alternating woven pattern locks cleanly around the open window.
Accordion-fold a 24 cm by 12 cm sheet back and forth along seven vertical creases into eight crisp 3 cm pleats.
With the pleats pressed flat, trim a pointed crest at the top and cut two staggered diamond notches into both folded side edges, keeping the center spine intact.
Pinch the bottom end of the pleated stack tightly inside a small folded paper collar clip and begin spreading the upper ribs outward.
Open the pleated fan a full 180 degrees so the alternating facets and stepped diamond openings stand upright and cast layered shadows.
Fold a 22 cm by 16 cm cardstock rectangle in half horizontally so the bottom edge meets the top edge along a crisp lower spine.
From the folded bottom spine, cut three pairs of vertical slits of staggered building heights (medium left, tall center, and stepped right) and crease horizontally across each top.
Unfold the sheet flat, trim a stepped silhouette along the upper backdrop edge, and cut small rectangular windows into the lower half of each building strip.
Open the backdrop 90 degrees to the base and push the three windowed building columns forward so the layered skyline stands proudly upright.
Cut eight identical 10 cm paper discs and fold each cleanly in half along its vertical diameter.
Stack the folded half-discs in alternating order: apply thin glue lines at top, middle, and bottom on odd layers, and at the one-quarter and three-quarter heights on even layers.
Once the stack holds together, snip two crisp V-notches into the outer curved edge between the green-marked glue bridges so every bridge stays intact.
Fan the stacked half-discs all the way around in a 360-degree circle and clip or glue the first and last faces together.
Lock the seam closed to display the full 3D honeycomb sphere with repeating diamond cells and scalloped outer edges.
Fold a 16 cm square cardstock sheet in half vertically so the left edge meets the right edge along a clean central spine.
From the folded spine, cut three concentric curved arch slots stopping 2 cm shy of the outer right edge so the side pier stays connected as a solid bridge.
Open the card slightly and push each cut arch band forward along its radial valley creases while keeping the outer frame bent in a wide V.
Stand the V-folded frame upright so the concentric valley-cut ribs spring forward into a vaulted three-tier paper arch.
Score vertical side-post borders and a 2 cm bottom stand flap on a 14 cm by 20 cm cardstock sheet, then snip three centered vertical starter slits between the posts.
Widen each starter slit into a rectangular trellis window while cutting around the alternating pointed ivy-leaf silhouettes, leaving each green-marked leaf stem connected to its rail.
Fold the side posts slightly backward, fold the bottom stand flap back 90 degrees, and tilt each cut ivy leaf gently forward along its stem bridge.
Stand the slot-cut ivy trellis upright on its angled side pillars and base ledge so the curling leaves frame the open lattice windows.
Cut a 12 cm radius semicircle and accordion-fold it back and forth along five radial lines from the top center into six equal 30-degree pleats.
With the radial wedge folded flat, snip two diagonal branch notches into the outer right edge and trim a stepped trunk corner at the bottom, leaving the left spine solid.
Unfold the pleated wedge smoothly outward so the fluted half-cone ribs open into three stepped bough tiers.
Stand the fluted 180-degree half-tree upright on its notched trunk base for a dimensional tabletop pine.
Fold a 16 cm square paper in half diagonally three times to form a crisp eight-layer 45-degree wedge with the closed center tip at the bottom.
Trim the top edge at a steep slant to shape the star point, then cut three alternating long and short radial fringe slits inward, stopping above the green-marked solid hub.
Unfold the eight-layer wedge completely flat to reveal the eight-pointed star ringed with alternating long and short fringe fingers.
Fold every second fringe ray slightly upward along its root bridge while keeping the alternate rays flat to give the star crisp 3D alternating relief.
