On a 16 cm by 22 cm cardstock sheet, mark a 3.5 cm bottom shelf fold, cut an inverted U-shaped kickstand tongue in the center, and cut two small front retaining tabs along the shelf line.
Push the rear kickstand tongue backward along its top hinge and fold the bottom shelf forward 90 degrees so the two retaining tabs stand straight up.
Rest a 10 cm square calendar card on the front shelf and slide its lower corners snugly behind the two upright retaining tabs.
Stand the easel upright on its rear kickstand and front ledge so the calendar card stays firmly clipped in place.
Fold a 14 cm by 22 cm sheet in half lengthwise so the left edge meets the right edge along a clean vertical center spine.
Punch a hanging hole near the top fold, then cut three nested teardrop curves from the spine, stopping just short of alternating top and bottom green-marked bridges.
Unfold the outer frame flat and gently twist each nested teardrop tier in alternating directions around its top and bottom bridge hinges.
Suspend the frame from its top hole so each alternating concentric silhouette tilts smoothly in space like a cascading paper mobile.
Cut a 5 x 8 cm floor with an attached 5 x 6.5 cm hinged arch door and tuck tab, a 5 x 6.5 cm notched back arch wall, an 8 x 16 cm roof-and-wall wrap with 1 cm end tabs, and a 3.5 cm signal flag.
Curl the center 8 cm section of the wrap smoothly around a dowel into an arch and crease both 1 cm bottom glue tabs inward 90 degrees.
Glue the inward tabs of the curved roof wrap onto the 5 x 8 cm floor edges, then fold and glue the notched back arch wall inside the rear opening.
Attach the 3.5 cm signal flag to the right side wall with a small split-pin brad, then crease the hinged front door upward along the floor edge.
Tuck the front door tab cleanly under the arched roof rim and swing the signal flag upright to complete your miniature mailbox.
Cut a 10 x 5.5 cm cardstock frame with a centered 5 x 2.8 cm window and 1.5 cm side tabs, a 7 x 4.6 cm backing card, and a 5.6 x 4 cm insert strip.
Crease both 1.5 cm side mounting tabs crisp along the frame edges, and dot glue along the left, right, and bottom edges of the backing card, leaving the top open.
Press the backing pocket behind the frame to form a sleeve, slide the blank label card into the top slot, and coat the outer side tabs with glue.
Press both glue tabs firmly against the drawer front so the framed label holds interchangeable paper strips cleanly.
Cut a 14 cm circle of lightweight craft paper, lightly trace a 5 cm circle at the center, and fold the disc cleanly in half.
Fold the circle in half three more times into a narrow 16-layer wedge, then trim a smooth rounded scallop arc across the outer edge.
Unfold the 16-scallop disc and pinch crisp radial mountain-and-valley creases from each scallop notch and tip inward to the 5 cm base ring.
Center the scalloped disc atop an inverted 5 cm cup and fold the pleated walls evenly down around the cylinder, overlapping each pleat cleanly.
Lift the shaped paper cup off the mold and flare the 16-scallop pleated rim gently outward to finish your cupcake liner.
Cut six 1.5 x 18 cm bell strips, one 1.5 x 22 cm rim band, one 3 cm crown disc, and five 0.8 x 20 cm narrow tentacle strips.
Glue the 22 cm rim band into a 7 cm ring with a 1 cm overlap, and wrap each narrow tentacle strip tightly around a pencil to form springy curls.
Glue all six 18 cm bell strips evenly across their midpoints onto the 3 cm crown disc to form a 12-arm star, and anchor a hanging cord loop at the center.
Arch each of the twelve radiating strip arms smoothly downward and glue their tips evenly spaced inside the 7 cm rim ring.
Glue the five curled ribbon tentacles evenly inside the rim ring and suspend your looped-paper jellyfish by its top cord.
Score a 13.5 x 36 cm cardstock sheet vertically into four 9 cm panels and horizontally 3.5 cm from the bottom, cutting small V-notches at the bottom fold intersections.
Fold the 3.5 cm bottom pocket strip cleanly upward along the horizontal crease across all four panels.
Apply thin glue dots along only the vertical side edges of each pocket flap so the tops stay open, then accordion-fold the four panels back and forth.
Stand the accordion booklet slightly fanned open and slide a 6.5 x 8 cm photo card into each open top pocket.
Stand the filled pocket photo album upright to display your mini gallery, or fold it flat and slip the 2 cm belly band around the covers.
Score a 24 x 16 cm cardstock sheet in half, cut a centered 7.5 x 11 cm window in the front panel, cut four corner slits and a bottom locking slot in the back panel, and score a 4 x 15 cm strut strip.
Slip an 8 x 11.5 cm photo cleanly into the four diagonal corner slits, then apply glue dots around the outer border of the windowed front half.
Fold the windowed front mat over the backing card along the center crease and press the glued borders flat around the framed photo.
Turn the mat face down, glue the top 2 cm tab of the 4 x 15 cm strut to the upper back center, and tuck its 1 cm bottom tab into the horizontal slot.
Set the folded photo mat upright on a desk so the locked rear triangular strut braces the frame at a crisp viewing angle.
Cut two 14 x 10 cm cover boards, three 14 x 10.5 cm divider cards with staggered top tabs, and two 4 x 24 cm side gusset strips scored every 1.5 cm.
Accordion-fold both 24 cm side gusset strips back and forth along the 1.5 cm score lines into springy zig-zag concertina pleats.
Dot glue on the rear outer pleat flaps of both folded gussets and attach them flush along the left and right edges of the back cover board.
Glue the three staggered tabbed dividers sequentially into the consecutive inward pleat valleys, then seal the front cover board to the front pleats.
Pull the covers apart to expand the pleated side gussets and file 12 x 9 cm recipe cards neatly behind the staggered divider tabs.
Cut a 16 x 14 cm cardstock base scored 2 cm from both left and right edges, then cut four parallel 10 cm slots spaced 2.5 cm apart across the floor.
Cut four 12 cm wide scene panels with matching 10 x 1.2 cm bottom tabs: a sunlit sky, a lighthouse cliff, a sailboat wave strip, and an arched foreground frame.
Fold both 2 cm side rails sharply upward 90 degrees along the scored edges to stiffen the slotted stage base into a steady tray.
Press the sky backdrop tab into the rearmost floor slot, then slide the lighthouse cliff and sailboat wave strip into the two middle slots.
Lock the foreground green harbor arch into the frontmost slot so all four planes stand upright with crisp theatrical depth.
Lightly mark sweeping sky, sun, hill, and river zones on a 15 x 12 cm cream backing board, then snip 1.5 cm colored paper strips at slight angles into irregular mosaic tiles.
Dot glue in the upper sky and corner sun zones and press blue and gold mosaic tiles in place, leaving narrow 2 mm cream gaps between every piece.
Arrange angled green tiles across the middle rolling hills and curve deep-blue tiles along the winding river channel, keeping even 2 mm grout spacing.
Fill the foreground meadow with warm peach and gold tiles, then glue 1.5 cm border strips cleanly around all four edges to frame your mosaic landscape.
Cut eight 1.2 x 16 cm globe ribbons punched 1 cm from both ends, six 1.2 x 14 cm chevron-notched tail ribbons, and two 1.5 x 6 cm collar bands.
Thread a 25 cm hanging cord through a small rolled top collar ring, stack all eight upper ribbon holes onto the cord, and secure a knot beneath the stack.
Fan the eight ribbons evenly in a circle, bow each ribbon outward into a rounded globe cage, and slide all eight bottom holes onto the lower cord.
Wrap and glue the second 1.5 x 6 cm gold collar band tightly around the lower ribbon junction to lock the bowed globe shape.
Glue the six chevron-notched ribbon tails evenly around the underside of the lower collar band and suspend your ornament by its top cord.
Cut 6 blue and 6 gold strips (1 cm wide by 18 cm long, 1:18 ratio) plus 2 narrow peach accent strips (0.5 cm by 18 cm), laying the blue set with one centered peach strip parallel at +45 degrees.
Weave the first three gold strips across at -45 degrees in an alternating over-one, under-one bias rhythm, keeping equal gaps between strips.
Weave the central peach pinstripe and remaining gold strips to finish the diagonal plaid, pack intersections tightly, and trim overhanging ends along a centered square border.
Glue a thin backing border behind the trimmed perimeter to lock all 14 bias strips into a crisp diagonal plaid mat.
Cut 8 vertical green warp strips (1.2 cm by 16 cm, ~1:13 ratio) and 6 horizontal gold weft strips (1.2 cm by 20 cm, ~1:17 ratio) of identical width.
Align the 8 vertical strips and weave row 1 symmetrically across the centerline (over-2, under-4, over-2); shift row 2 inward by one column on both halves to launch the V-shaped chevron.
Continue mirroring each new row inward by one strip for all 6 rows to form stacked herringbone chevrons, pack tight, then fold and glue overhanging ends behind the mat.
Press the completed herringbone mat flat under a book until dry so the symmetrical chevron ridges stay crisp.
Cut a 4 cm green center disc with 6 radial slits spaced 60 degrees apart, and cut 6 alternating gold and peach strips (1.5 cm by 16 cm, ~1:11 ratio) with short 1 cm end tabs.
Bend each strip into a wide teardrop loop, bringing both creased end tabs together and flaring the 1 cm feet outward.
Slide the paired base tabs of each teardrop loop into one radial slit of the green center hub until the flared feet catch underneath.
Interlock the wide outer petals cyclically—tucking each loop over its clockwise neighbor and under its counter-clockwise neighbor—then flatten the locking tabs behind the hub.
Cut 12 equal strips (1 cm by 22 cm, 1:22 ratio): 4 blue, 4 gold, and 4 peach. Arrange the 4 blue strips horizontally with even 1.4 cm spacing.
Slide the 4 gold strips across at +60 degrees underneath all four horizontal blue strips, spacing them equally to form a diamond grid.
Weave the 4 peach strips across at -60 degrees—passing OVER blue and UNDER gold—to lock the tri-axial hexagon windows, then trim the outer tails along a hexagonal perimeter.
Pack the tri-axial weave evenly toward the center and glue tiny dots at the perimeter intersections to finish a self-braced hexagonal lattice coaster.
Cut 8 vertical green ribs (1.2 cm by 16 cm, ~1:13 ratio) and 4 long horizontal hoop bands (1.2 cm by 22 cm, ~1:18 ratio) alternating gold and peach.
Space the 8 green vertical ribs evenly with 0.8 cm gaps and weave the first two bands over-one, under-one across the bottom half to leave open square lattice windows.
Roll the flat woven sheet into an upright cylinder and glue the overlapping ends of both lower bands by 1.5 cm to close the cylindrical base.
Weave the upper two bands in alternating over/under tension around the upper ribs and glue each band's overlap cleanly behind a rib to finish an airy latticed sleeve.
Cut 6 alternating blue, gold, and peach strips (2.2 cm by 16 cm, ~1:7 ratio) and slice a centered 1.8 cm longitudinal eye-slit 1.5 cm from each end.
Curve the first blue strip softly into a U-loop—without creasing the rounded belly—so both end eye-slits align together into one double-layered slot.
Slip the rounded center fold of a gold strip through the aligned eye-slits of the blue loop, then flare the gold arms slightly so the slit collar locks in place.
Continue threading alternating loops through each preceding pair of eye-slits in a gentle wave to finish a glue-free horizontal interlocking-eye garland.
Cut a 10 cm by 12 cm stiff backing card, 1 long plum border strip (0.6 cm by 34 cm), and 10 narrow filigree strips (0.6 cm by 18 cm, 1:30 ratio) in gold and peach.
Crease the plum border strip into a symmetrical hexagonal shield frame, glue its overlapping ends, and mount it edge-on onto the backing card.
Roll the narrow gold and peach strips tightly into coils, let them relax slightly into open spirals, and pinch two coils into crisp teardrop shapes.
Pack the teardrop loops and spiral scrolls symmetrically inside the raised plum shield cavity, edge-gluing contact points until the filigree fills the crest.
Cut 7 vertical blue warp strips (1.4 cm by 24 cm, ~1:17 ratio) and 5 horizontal gold weft strips (1.4 cm by 30 cm, ~1:21 ratio) with generous 4 cm extra length on every end.
Weave all 5 gold weft strips over-one, under-one across the 7 blue warp strips, centering the 7x5 grid so 4 cm tails protrude evenly on all four sides.
Crease all protruding left and right gold tails 180 degrees around the outer blue columns and tuck each tip cleanly beneath the second column's cross-strip to build doubled side selvedges.
With the side selvedges locked, fold the top and bottom blue tails 180 degrees over the outer gold rows and tuck each tip under the second row.
Press all four folded selvedges flat so the doubled border rim stays thick, self-locked, and fray-free without any raw cut strip ends.

Cut 8 radial rib strips (1.8 cm by 24 cm, ~1:13 ratio) in alternating peach and gold with four shallow side notches on each arm, plus 2 blue hoop bands (1.8 cm by 28 cm) with 8 evenly spaced half-width slots.
Cross all 8 radial strips cleanly at their midpoints in a balanced 16-arm starburst, alternating overlaps around an 8 cm octagonal base hub.
Curve the 16 rib arms smoothly upward into a flared bowl wall and slide the first slotted blue band onto the mid-height notches around the outside.
Seat the second slotted blue band over the upper rim notches of all 16 ribs and interlock its overlapping ends to tension the bowl.
Evenly adjust the flared peach and gold rib spacing around both slotted blue rings to complete a sturdy, glue-minimal fluted strip bowl.
Cut three stepped strips—inner plum (3 cm by 16 cm), middle gold (4 cm by 20 cm), and outer peach (5 cm by 24 cm)—and mark a 0.8 cm uncut spine line along the bottom of each.
Cut fine parallel fringe slits every 4 mm from the top edge down to the dashed 0.8 cm spine margin on all three strips without cutting through the bottom spine.
Stack the three fringed strips flush along their bottom spines (plum shortest in front, gold middle, peach longest behind), glue the spines together, and roll tightly from the plum end.
Glue the outer peach spine tab securely, then fan and splay the peach skirt flat, arch the gold tier outward, and fluff the inner plum center tuft upright.
Shape the concentric tiers evenly all around the rolled core to reveal a full, three-color compound fringe paper pom.
Start with a 15 x 11 cm rectangle. Valley-fold the top and bottom edges inward to meet along the center line.
Pleat lengthwise along the center valley and two outer mountain creases to raise a central V-channel between two angled legs.
Fold all four bottom leg corners diagonally inward at 45 degrees to lock the bridge angle and prevent the legs from splaying.
Gently widen the upper V-cradle and press the four folded feet level onto the desk to support a pencil.
Start with a square sheet. Valley-fold both side margins inward by one-tenth to stiffen the scoop rails.
Valley-fold the tapered side walls and back wall upward together so the front lip stays low and beveled.
Fold the two triangular corner gussets flat against the back wall, then fold the top cuffs down over them to lock the corners.
Fold the center back tab outward into a finger grip while pressing the front edge flat to sweep crumbs.
Start with a square sheet rotated like a diamond. Valley-fold the bottom corner up to meet the top corner.
Fold only the front top corner straight down to touch the midpoint of the bottom folded edge.
Valley-fold both the left and right corners upward along the diagonal creases so their tips meet at the top point.
Fold both upper wing tips downward and tuck them neatly behind the front triangular pocket flap to lock the page sleeve.
Start with a 18 x 12 cm rectangular sheet. Valley-fold both short outer margins inward to build crisp side retainer cuffs.
Valley-fold the lower two-fifths of the sheet upward to form the deep front pocket for a gift card.
Fold the top-left and top-right flap corners diagonally inward at 45 degrees to taper a locking tongue.
Swing the tapered top flap down over the front rim and tuck the beveled tongue cleanly inside the pocket to lock without clips.
Start with a tall 9 x 16 cm sheet colored-side down. Valley-fold the left third inward across the middle.
Valley-fold the right third inward to overlap the left panel and form a crisp three-layer sleeve body.
Fold the upper corner of the top overlapping panel diagonally downward to create the traditional angled chopstick collar.
Fold the bottom end upward along the lower crease and slip its tip behind the front wrap edge to seal the sleeve.
Start with a 22 x 9 cm paper strip. Valley-fold the top and bottom edges inward to create double-thick cuffs along the band.
Accordion-pleat six vertical ribs across the middle section to build a textured, insulating grip.
Fold the right-end corners diagonally inward to taper a locking tongue, then curve both ends forward into a C-ring.
Wrap the band into a closed cylinder and slide the tapered locking tongue inside the opposite cuff pocket to lock the cup sleeve.
Start with a 15 x 15 cm square colored side down. Valley-fold the top and bottom edges inward to meet along the horizontal centerline.
Valley-fold both right-hand halves symmetrically outward along angled creases from the center notch to spread the two whale-tail fluke tips.
Mountain-fold the two protruding fluke points neatly behind along the outer edges to round the forked tail silhouette.
Valley-fold the left vertical edge inward 1.7 cm to create a crisp contrasting mast cuff for the Whale-Tail Flag.
Gently pinch the horizontal centerline forward so the banner lifts into a dimensional wave with twin notched flukes.
Start with a 15 x 15 cm square rotated like a diamond with the colored side down. Valley-fold the bottom corner straight up to the top corner.
Valley-fold the left corner diagonally upward along the crease to lift the baby bird's upright neck and head.
Valley-fold the right corner diagonally upward to raise a short stubby tail on the opposite side.
Valley-fold the top tip of the raised neck forward and left to form a small pointed chick beak.
Mountain-fold the upper back point behind to round the bird's plump torso, stand it on its level base, and add a small eye dot.
Start with a 15 x 15 cm square colored side up. Valley-fold the top edge straight down to the bottom edge.
Open the front pocket slightly and tuck both upper corners inward along the diagonals to collapse into a triangle Waterbomb Base.
Valley-fold ONLY the two front triangle flaps steeply upward along the inner creases to form two raised crab pincers.
Valley-fold the remaining two rear corners outward at a wider angle to splay the crab's side walking legs.
Mountain-fold the center top peak behind the body to round the crab's wide carapace.
Flip the model over to the smooth coral side and add two small eyes along the front rim.
Start with a 15 x 15 cm square rotated like a diamond with the colored side down. Valley-fold both lower edges inward, leaving a crisp light belly stripe down the center.
Valley-fold the top white peak straight down across the brow line to form the penguin's dark head and pointed beak.
Mountain-fold the two upper outer shoulders behind the head to round the penguin's crown.
Valley-fold the bottom point upward to form a level sitting base and dark feet rim.
Angle both dark side wing flaps slightly backward so the Sitting Penguin stands upright, then add two small eyes.
Start with a 15 x 15 cm square rotated like a diamond with the colored side down. Valley-fold the bottom corner up to the top corner.
Mountain-fold the top peak straight down behind the horizontal brow line so the tip extends slightly below as a pointed tail.
Valley-fold both outer side wings upward and inward along symmetric creases to leave two pointed bat ears along the top edge.
Pleat-fold both raised wing tips back outward so the wide scalloped bat wings sweep cleanly to the sides.
Slightly angle both outstretched wings forward in a soaring V-pose and add two tiny eyes beneath the brow.
Start with a 15 x 15 cm square colored side down, rotated horizontally like a diamond. Valley-fold both left edges inward to meet along the center spine.
Valley-fold the upper-right and lower-right edges symmetrically inward to taper the pangolin's long armored tail.
Make a crisp vertical valley-and-mountain pleat across the mid-back so the armor bands overlap along the spine.
Mountain-fold the lower half behind the upper half along the horizontal centerline to form the arched profile.
Valley-fold the tapered left tip slightly downward for the pangolin's snout and angle the right tail tip gently behind.
Tuck the small lower chest corner behind to shape a tucked foreleg ledge and add a small eye near the snout.
Take a 14 cm × 20 cm sheet of cardstock and fold it in half horizontally along the center crease to form an A-frame spine.
Unfold flat and cut two 6.6 cm locking tabs along the lower outer margins of the back panel, stopping 6 mm above the bottom edge so each tab hinges cleanly.
Cut a centered arch cutout along the bottom edge of the front panel and slice two matching horizontal locking slots 6 mm above the front corners.
Stand the creased sign upright into a 40° A-frame while folding both back locking tabs forward toward horizontal.
Guide both locking tabs forward through the matching front corner slots so their tapered tips catch and hold the desk sign upright.
Fold a 6 cm × 36 cm gold strip into six equal 6 cm accordion pleats, alternating mountain and valley creases.
Cut the top profile across the folded stack: trace an upright half-bell crown down from the left fold, keep a 1.3 cm center bridge, then cut up around the inverted bell rim to the right fold.
Cut the mirrored bottom profile from the left fold around the bell rim and under the center bridge to the inverted bell crown on the right fold, leaving both fold bridges uncut.
Unfold the pleated stack outward to reveal the continuous garland of alternating upright and inverted linked bells.

lessons.name: Folding Bridge Card with Supported Deck

steps.instruction: Take a 22 cm × 12 cm blue card scored into a 12 cm back wall and two 5 cm wings; fold both wings forward 90° and mark the vertical wing slots.
On a 12 cm × 9 cm gold bridge sheet, cut a centered semicircular arch out of the lower edge and keep the side locking tabs intact.
Fold the two under-deck support piers inward 90° beneath the span, then fold the horizontal roadway deck down 90° to rest on top of the piers.
Slide the bridge end tabs smoothly into the matching vertical wing slots until the supported bridge deck sits level across the card.
Test the parallelogram fold: press the side wings sideways so the supported deck tucks flat for an envelope, then pull open into a standing 3D bridge.
Fold a 14 cm × 18 cm coral sheet in half vertically along the center spine.
Trim diagonally across the top and bottom outer corners of the folded stack to create a tapered octagonal lantern profile.
From the folded center spine, cut five evenly spaced parallel chevron slits stopping 2.4 cm short of the outer rim to keep narrow hinge bridges.
Unfold the lantern flat to reveal the nested chevron ribs centered inside the octagonal frame.
Push and fold alternating chevron ribs forward and backward 68° through the frame opening while gently creasing the center spine for a 3D hanging decor ornament.
Cut away the upper-left and upper-right shoulder strips on a 16 cm × 13 cm teal cardstock sheet to leave a centered 5.6 cm top index tab.
Cut the outer 2.8 cm horizontal wing slits 4 cm from the bottom edge, snip spaced perforation slits along the center fold line and side wing hinges, and cut a front U-slit for the center stop-tab.
Fold the main tabbed divider upright 90° along the horizontal perforation line while keeping the base foot flat.
Fold both side stabilizer wings up 90° along their vertical perforations and tilt the perforated front stop-tab up 90° to support cards.
Take a 5.5 cm × 16.5 cm plum cardstock strip and trim both top corners diagonally to form a pointed crown.
Fold the bookmark strip in half lengthwise along the vertical center crease.
Cut a centered V-notch from the folded upper spine, remove the triangular offcut, and unfold flat to reveal a diamond cutout window.
Below the diamond window, cut a pointed U-shaped slit stopping at the top horizontal bridge to free the hinged flip tab.
Flip the hinged tab forward along its top bridge to reveal the cream reverse face and settle it at a page-clipping angle.
Cut two 15 x 5 cm teal cardstock strips and one 13.5 x 6 cm gold base card.
Roll each 15 x 5 cm strip into a tight 2 cm diameter tube and glue the tail edge shut.
Glue both rolled tubes side by side 0.5 cm apart on the base card to form a pen cradle.
Fold the 1.5 cm left and right base flaps upright against the twin rolls to lock the pen rest.
Accordion-fold a 14 x 9 cm sage sheet lengthwise into crisp 1 cm alternating pleats.
Press the pleats together and trim a curved 45-degree leaf taper from both upper corners.
Glue the center spine seam together and fan the pleats open into a 3D leaf.
Stand three graduated leaves (14, 12, and 10 cm tall) upright and thread cords through 2 mm tip holes.
Slide the three knotted cords into 3 mm notches spaced 6 cm apart on a 20 cm folded crossbar.

lessons.name: Layered Standing Picture with Slot Base

steps.instruction: Cut the 14 x 10 cm sky panel with a 3 cm sun disc, 14 x 7.5 cm hill panel, and 14 x 5 cm ridge panel.
Fold two 10 x 1.5 cm Z-spacer strips and glue them between the three picture panels 8 mm apart.
Cut three 12 cm x 2 mm parallel slots spaced 1.4 cm apart in a 16 x 7 cm plinth card and fold its 1 cm side skirts down.
Slide the spaced three-layer picture straight down into the matching base slots until seated upright.

lessons.name: Two-Part Low Paper Basket with Handle

steps.instruction: Score an 18 x 18 cm peach square 4 cm from each edge, cut four 4 cm corner slits, and cut a 26 x 2.5 cm pine handle strip.
Fold all four 4 cm walls upright 82 degrees and hinge the four 4 cm corner glue tabs inward.
Apply glue to the four corner tabs and press them flush inside the adjacent basket walls.
Fold 2 cm mounting tabs at both ends of the 26 x 2.5 cm strip and curve the center into an arch.
Glue both 2 cm handle tabs firmly onto the center inside faces of opposite basket walls.
Cut a 20 x 7 cm indigo tag blank with beveled shoulders, a 4 x 2.5 cm window cutout, and a 5 mm top eyelet.
Fold both 1.2 cm side pocket flaps 180 degrees inward onto the lower back panel.
Fold the windowed front panel upward 180 degrees over the side flaps and tuck the top collar into the pocket.
Slide the 6 x 4.5 cm cream info card down into the pocket behind the front window frame.
Pass the 20 x 1.2 cm coral strap through the 5 mm eyelet and thread its tail through the end slit to lock the loop.

lessons.name: Windup-Look Paper Flower with Split Pin

steps.instruction: Cut a 9 cm six-petal coral flower, 11 cm six-point sage calyx, 14 x 2.2 cm leafy stem, and 5 x 3.5 cm gold windup key.
Cup each coral petal 18 degrees forward and fold the two 2.5 cm wings of the gold windup key 90 degrees upright.
Stack the coral flower over the sage calyx and stem top, then push an 8 mm brass split pin through the 3 mm center holes.
Slide the gold windup key onto the split-pin shaft behind the stem and splay both brass legs flat outward to lock the pivot.
Turn the gold windup key from behind to rotate the six-petal coral flower smoothly on its brass split-pin axle.
Cut a 2.4 cm by 16 cm sage cardstock strip with a narrow neck and flared arrowhead tab on the right, then slice a 1.4 cm transverse slit near the left end.
Score both angled shoulder creases and valley-fold the two arrowhead wings upward so the tip narrows to fit through the slit.
Curl the strip smoothly into a closed teardrop loop, guiding the folded arrowhead tip around to sit directly over the open slit.
Thread the narrowed arrowhead tip through the slit from outside to inside, then unfold both wings flat underneath to lock the cable keeper.
Cut six 1.2 cm by 22 cm strips—two teal, two gold, and two coral—with 45° mitered starting tips, and align three parallel at +45°.
Weave the three opposing -45° strips across the +45° strips in alternating over-one, under-one bias order to lock the lower diamond.
Fold each strip emerging from the left and right edges 90° inward along the vertical border, weaving every turn over-and-under up the column.
Fold the top tails behind into a crisp pointed pennant tip, trim the excess triangles flush, and secure underneath with a glue dot.
Cut six longer coral rib strips (1.2 cm by 18 cm) and six shorter teal spine strips (1.2 cm by 14 cm), plus two sage collar bands.
Glue all twelve alternating strips along the bottom sage collar, then slide the top collar down to 14 cm so the longer coral strips arch outward.
Curve the assembled ribbed sheet smoothly into an upright cylinder and join both overlapping sage collar rings.
Weave a gold equator band around the drum—passing underneath every bowed coral rib and over every flat teal spine—and tuck its tab.

lessons.name: Woven Two-Pocket Wallet with Taped Backing

steps.instruction: Lay ten vertical blue warp strips side by side and weave six horizontal gold weft strips in alternating over-one, under-one plain weave.
Fold all overhanging blue and gold ends onto the back face and press overlapping craft tape strips across the sheet for a smooth taped backing.
Fold the lower half upward onto the taped backing and tape the left edge, right edge, and center seam to divide two side-by-side card pockets.
Crease down the vertical centerline and fold the right wing over the left to close the woven two-pocket wallet.
Curve a coral strip (1.6 cm by 22 cm) into an open U-bight and bring a matching gold strip across the upper-right leg.
Weave the gold strip cleanly through the coral loop in strict over-under-over-under Carrick-bend order across all four crossings.
Pull the four ends evenly outward to tighten the center diamond and round both outer coral and gold lobes.
Curve the paired tails inward to close the lower and right lobes, tuck every trimmed tip behind the opposite collar band, and add a crown hanging loop.
Cut seven 1.8 cm by 18 cm strips—four teal and three gold—with 45° diagonal beveled top tips, plus one narrow coral linking ribbon.
Stack all seven blades with base pivot holes aligned, insert a rolled sage paper pin through the hub, and flare both pin tabs flat.
Spread the blades partway open and weave the narrow coral ribbon diagonally from lower-left to upper-right in alternating over-under order.
Spread the outer teal guard blades wide open to 130° until the woven coral ribbon pulls taut along its rising diagonal arc.
Push both outer blades smoothly back together so the diagonal ribbon accordion-pleats cleanly inside and the fan folds shut into a compact wand.
Cut out the triangular sleeve net, inner drawer tray net, and pull-tab strip from 200 gsm cardstock, trimming away the outer waste strips cleanly along the dashed cut guides.
Valley-fold the two sloped sleeve walls 120° inward, fold up the triangular back end cap 90° with its side tabs, and glue the top seam tab to form the hollow triangular cover.
Fold the inner drawer's sloped side cheeks 120° inward, raise the triangular front faceplate and trapezoidal back wall 90°, and glue their side tabs inside.
Glue the pull-tab mount flush onto the front triangular faceplate and crease the horizontal pull tongue 90° outward with a small finger lip.
Align the finished triangular drawer with the sleeve opening and slide it smoothly inside using the front pull tab.
Cut out the four-sided pyramid perch stand net and the symmetrical swept-wing bird net from 200 gsm cardstock, separating the wingtip trim scraps cleanly.
Valley-fold all four triangular stand walls upward to meet at a sharp perch apex and glue the seam tabs inside to form a sturdy desk pedestal.
Mountain-fold the bird's central spine ridge downward 36° on each side to form a V-shaped chest keel, and crease both rear tail fins slightly upward.
Angle both swept-forward wings along the shoulder creases so the forward wingtips dip slightly below the chest keel for low center-of-gravity balance.
Set the bird's forward chest point onto the pyramid perch apex and release gently so the swept wings balance the sculpture level.
Cut out the sloped open cradle net, two vertical fore-aft partition fins, and the lateral cross-divider bar, trimming out the matching half-height interlock slots cleanly.
Fold the tall back wall, low front rim, and sloped side walls 90° upward, gluing the front and rear side tabs inside to form an open tabletop tray.
Lower the two slotted vertical partition fins upright into the tray cradle along the left and right third lines with their slots facing upward.
Press the lateral cross-divider straight down so its two downward notches interlock flush with the partition fin slots to create six compartments.
Fold the left and right coral end locking flaps 90° against the inner side walls to brace the slotted grid cleanly without glue on the dividers.
Cut out both two-panel rectangular shade halves (decor only) with their wide connector straps and centered decorative window cutouts, removing the inner window offcuts cleanly.
Fold the peach front and right walls 90° into a crisp corner and crease both wide coral connector tongues 84° around the outer corners.
Fold the sage back and left walls 90° into the matching opposite corner and crease both wide inner collar tabs 96° inward.
Slide the two L-shaped halves together so both wide connector tongues engage inside the opposing collar straps to lock the decorative rectangular shade.
Cut out the hollow trapezoidal beam net (with end-diaphragm flaps) and two bridge pier abutment nets from 200 gsm cardstock, trimming the diagonal relief notches cleanly.
Fold both bridge pier nets 90° into rectangular abutment blocks, gluing the side tabs inside and closing the top bearing caps.
Fold the bridge beam's sloped web walls 66° upward and fold both top deck halves 114° inward over the glued center seam tab to form a hollow box girder.
Fold both trapezoidal end-diaphragm flaps 90° upright into the beam ends and glue their side tabs inside the sloped webs to keep the hollow section rigid.
Set the stiffened hollow beam squarely across both pier abutments, then lower the folded paper test block onto mid-span to load-test the beam.
Cut out the wrap-around book cover net with its central boxed spine and mitered turn-in flaps, snipping away the four outer corner triangles cleanly.
Fold the top and bottom turn-in tabs 170° inward onto the back and front cover boards, then fold both fore-edge pocket flaps inward over them.
Glue the fore-edge pocket flaps onto the top and bottom turn-ins to form inner sleeves, then valley-fold both parallel spine hinges 90° upright.
Slide the folded cream folio pages cleanly into the spine cradle and swing the hinged front cover panel smoothly across to wrap the book.
